keyVerseText: Then said the LORD unto Isaiah, Go forth now to meet Ahaz, thou, and Shearjashub thy son, at the end of the conduit of the upper pool in the highway of the fuller's field; Shearjashub: that is, The remnant shall return highway: or, causeway
rootMeaning: The term שְׁאָר יָשׁוּב (Shear-Jashub) is composed of two Hebrew roots: שְׁאָר (shᵉʼâr), meaning 'remnant' or 'remainder,' and שׁוּב (yâshûwb), meaning 'will return.' Together, they literally convey the idea of 'a remnant shall return.' This etymology deepens the English gloss by emphasizing not just a leftover portion but an active, hopeful return of that remnant, highlighting restoration and continuity rather than mere survival.
usageInScripture: This proper name appears only once explicitly in Scripture, in Isaiah 7:3, where Shear-Jashub is identified as the son of the prophet Isaiah. The translation 'thou and Shearjashub' captures the personal name but also carries its symbolic meaning, 'a remnant shall return.' This singular usage as a symbolic name underscores its theological weight rather than a broad lexical range, focusing on the hope of God's preserving remnant amid judgment.
theologicalSignificance: Shear-Jashub, meaning 'a remnant shall return,' embodies a profound theological truth central to Scripture: despite judgment and exile, God preserves a faithful remnant who will be restored. This concept reassures believers of God's covenant faithfulness and His redemptive plan through hardship. It points forward to the ultimate restoration in Christ, who gathers His people and brings them back into fellowship with God. Recognizing this word's original meaning helps believers trust in God's sovereign preservation and the promise of spiritual renewal.
keyVerseReflection: Isaiah 7:3 commands Isaiah to meet King Ahaz accompanied by his son Shearjashub, whose name is explained as 'The remnant shall return.' This naming is not incidental but serves as a prophetic sign that even in the midst of political crisis, God's plan includes the preservation and return of a faithful remnant. The word Shear-Jashub enriches the verse by transforming the meeting into a living symbol of hope and restoration promised by God.
